key_insight: A mixed Petrov–Galerkin Cosserat rod FEM with linear kinematics and midpoint/trapezoidal quadrature can be recast as a two-node discrete rod with compliant force/moment couplings and no locking.
engineering_relevance: The formulation offers a robust, graphically intuitive rod model for soft robotics and slender-structure simulation while preserving FEM accuracy and convergence.
method: Represent the rod as rigid-body nodes connected by elastic interactions.
Compute dilatation, shear, torsion, and curvature from relative node kinematics.
Use compliance-based constitutive laws with independent stress DOFs and mixed FEM quadrature (midpoint/trapezoidal).
evidence_signal: The abstract reports three numerical examples—varying cross sections, tendon-driven actuation, and coupled longitudinal-torsional dynamics—showing accuracy, robustness, and convergence.
watch_item: Because the discrete model comes from a specific mixed FEM setup and quadrature choice, implementation must preserve the coupling and integration scheme to retain the no-locking behavior.
paper_title: A Mixed Discrete Cosserat Rod Formulation
